Change c0396. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XXI.

Context before (unchanged): His companions came up to assist him; and, by the light of their lantern, they found that he had fallen on the body of a man, who was to all appearance dead.

1818 text: Their first supposition was, that it was the corpse of some person who had been drowned, and was thrown on shore by the waves; but, upon examination, they found that the clothes were not wet, and even that the body was not then cold.

1831 text: Their first supposition was, that it was the corpse of some person who had been drowned, and was thrown on shore by the waves; but, on examination, they found that the clothes were not wet, and even that the body was not then cold.

Diff: Their first supposition was, that it was the corpse of some person who had been drowned, and was thrown on shore by the waves; but, [-upon-] {+on+} examination, they found that the clothes were not wet, and even that the body was not then cold.

Context after (unchanged): They instantly carried it to the cottage of an old woman near the spot, and endeavoured, but in vain, to restore it to life.

result.rationale: Replacing 'upon examination' with 'on examination' is a minor phrasal change in diction with no effect on meaning, events, or characterization.
